focus: security: --track path containment and card write-scope alignment

findingDetails.title: --track can route scaffold writes above the repository root
findingDetails.description: The --track value is accepted verbatim and appended to REPO_ROOT/specs before mkdir -p; traversal segments can move the scaffold destination above the repository root.
findingDetails.evidence: The parser only checks that --track has a value and assigns it to TRACK at create.sh:137-148. create.sh:1290-1294 interpolates TRACK into SPECS_DIR and creates that directory. create.sh:2096-2111 derives FEATURE_DIR and creates the scaffold there. This path does not pass through resolve_and_validate_create_target.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve the track and final scaffold destination before the first mkdir, then fail unless the canonical destination remains beneath REPO_ROOT/specs.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The phase 005 card explicitly invokes create.sh with --track and sets the authoring write boundary to the packet and scratch folders. This is the command implementation used by that in-scope card.
findingDetails.case: With --track ../../outside, SPECS_DIR becomes REPO_ROOT/specs/../../outside. After the script changes to REPO_ROOT, mkdir -p creates a directory above the repository; FEATURE_DIR then appends the generated packet name and template files are written there.

findingDetails.title: The authoring card omits the tracked scaffold metadata write
findingDetails.description: The card limits allowed writes to the packet and scratch folders, while a normal tracked scaffold also refreshes children_ids in the track root graph-metadata.json.
findingDetails.evidence: The card lists packet and scratch as its allowed writes at lines 20-25 and directs the reader to pass --track at lines 49-57. create.sh:1031-1042 runs refresh-track-roots.mjs with --apply for an existing single-segment track, which writes graph-metadata.json at refresh-track-roots.mjs:103-105. The spec README documents this create.sh --track side effect at lines 91 and 105.
findingDetails.recommendation: State the script-managed track-root metadata update as an explicit scaffold exception in the card, or adjust the scaffold flow so its writes match the card boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The phase 005 target creates the card, and the card itself defines the authoring write boundary for the tracked create.sh command.
findingDetails.case: A valid track with graph-metadata.json is used in the documented command; create.sh creates the packet and then refreshes the track root children_ids outside the new packet folder.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: The target is a multi-phase spec packet with a documented scaffold command and named implementation paths; this pass traced the track input through its filesystem writes.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A user-controlled --track value may escape the canonical specs tree before scaffold writes begin.
searchLedger.rationale: The raw value flows into SPECS_DIR and the created FEATURE_DIR without the explicit-path containment resolver.

searchActions.result: The parser assigns TRACK directly; explicit target validation is a separate path.

searchActions.queryOrPath: TRACK to SPECS_DIR to FEATURE_DIR and scaffold mkdir
searchActions.result: The path segments reach mkdir -p before any canonical containment check.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The documented card write boundary may omit a side effect of the tracked scaffold command.
searchLedger.rationale: The card names packet and scratch as the allowed write locations; the scaffold refreshes the track-root metadata file after creating the packet.

searchActions.result: The allowed-write list is narrower than the documented --track command behavior.

searchActions.queryOrPath: create.sh track refresh to metadata writer
searchActions.result: The script invokes the root refresh with --apply; the writer persists the changed children_ids.

targetSelection.selectionReason: The card is the phase 005 deliverable; its documented --track command leads to create.sh, and the metadata refresh is its named tracked-scaffold side effect. Coverage graph output is unavailable in this confined lineage.
